blockers: Normal daily run for 2026-11-10. GitHub Trending rendered 11 entries; all 11 were reviewed and star counts verified via the GitHub API.

Five coding-agent-eligible repos (>=3000 stars) on today's list: anthropics/skills (5), vercel-labs/agent-browser (5), anthropics/claude-quickstarts (4), garrytan/gbrain (4), homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp (3). Exactly 5, so the 5-per-day cap was used fully with nothing left over. The other 6 entries were rejected (OSINT tool, design-system library, physics simulator, WiFi sensing, stock-analysis app, end-user agent-host app).

Never re-clone rule applied: check_unmodified passed for all three already-archived repos before the same-volume move. anthropics/skills and claude-quickstarts were unchanged; agent-browser was upgraded 4b0e9f0 -> e751995 by incremental git fetch, previous manifests kept as previous-*.json. Nothing moved to Trash; no user-edited copies found.

git-lfs is still not installed on this Mac; none of today's archived trees contain LFS pointers. ha-mcp's one submodule (src/ha_mcp/resources/skills-vendor) was fetched at its pinned commit. Repository code, hooks, installers and dependencies were never run.
One new featured recommendation: garrytan/gbrain (never featured). ha-mcp was saved but not featured: it is only useful with a Home Assistant install.

featured.reason: GBrain (MIT, Bun/TypeScript): self-hosted agent memory with provenance, corrections and withdrawal, exposed through one CLI and an MCP server; keyless local start on PGLite (no server or Docker), keyword search first, optional embeddings, synthesis and a typed knowledge graph. Ships a guide for adding memory to Claude Code/Codex and a shared skills catalog. Useful as a portable memory layer across coding agents; heavy optional features (enrichment daemons, cloud providers) need careful scoping.
ideas: Start keyless on the Mac mini (`gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding`), then `gbrain import` only the archive's MEMORY.md and run reports with `--no-embed`, so any agent can ask `gbrain search` which repos were already featured instead of grepping a 200 KB file.
Follow docs/tutorials/connect-coding-agent.md to give Claude Code and Codex the same memory, and test it with one `gbrain remember` / `gbrain recall` round trip in two different sessions.

Store durable project facts for ai-daily-radar (keep the original non-glass design, WebView app loads the live site, daily 10 AM publish) with provenance, so new agents stop re-asking or undoing past decisions.

Read docs/architecture (PGLite vs Postgres + pgvector, one BrainEngine contract shared by CLI and MCP) to learn a clean pattern for a local-first data layer you could reuse in a web or mobile app with offline sync.

Try `gbrain mcp expose` on your Tailscale network in a sandboxed test brain and see whether your Android phone or a cloud agent can query notes safely; read the sharing-boundaries doc first and keep enrichment and paid providers off.

news_highlights.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Anthropic's new top model is cheaper ($8/$40 per million tokens), up to 30% faster, and leads its agentic-coding benchmarks. Anthropic still suggests Opus 5.5 as the daily driver and Fable for the hardest jobs, so pick models per task.

news_highlights.title: Claude Fable 5.2 scores 65 on artificial analysis, highest so far
news_highlights.why_it_matters: An independent leaderboard puts Fable 5.2 first, which backs up Anthropic's own numbers. Worth checking its cost per task before switching your coding agent over.

news_highlights.title: Beyond code generation: A developer's guide to agentic engineering
news_highlights.why_it_matters: GitHub says commits are up over 400% in a year while AI-heavy PRs wait much longer in review. The fix it suggests: smaller stacked PRs, automated checks, and agents across plan, build, verify and observe.

news_highlights.title: What's new in Node.js 27
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Node now ships one major a year and every release becomes LTS. The 27 alpha adds Iterator.zip, Math.sumPrecise, an unflagged node:vfs and --allow-env, and makes req.headers null-prototype, so add it to CI early.
